podcasts.title: Ep 93: CEO of Redwood Research Buck Shlegeris on OpenAI/HuggingFace Revelations, Fixing AI Safety & Takeover Odds
podcasts.transcript:
Speaker 1 | 00:00 - 00:37
The OpenAI Hugging Face incident has dominated the discourse these past days. It feels straight out of a sci fi novel, some of the things that happened, you know, the agent coordination, the obsession with the scores, and and what they would want. And we had the perfect person on today to just discuss everything that happened and the implications for AI safety going forward in Buck Schlegeris, who's the CEO of Redwood Research. Redwood was deeply involved in the creation of the report that you all have probably seen around what actually happened in this incident. And Buck had some fascinating takes on what lessons we should take away from, you know, what went wrong here and how it can inform AI safety going forward.

Speaker 1 | 00:37 - 01:01
I'm Jacob Efron, and on unsupervised learning, we're always trying to talk with people at the cutting edge about what AI means for society, the implications for the world going forward, and this was really just a great example of that conversation. Just a fascinating discussion with Buck about something that I'm sure is top of mind for all of our listeners. Without further ado, here's our conversation. Well, Buck, thanks so much for for joining the podcast. Really appreciate it.

Speaker 2 | 01:01 - 01:02
Yeah. It's good to be here.

Speaker 1 | 01:02 - 01:42
Yeah. Well, obviously, you know, you you run Redwood Research. You've done a a bunch of fascinating work over the years, and your team kind of co authored the report that I feel like has been on the tip of everyone's tongue these past days, you know, really driving the discourse around what happened in this opening eye, hugging face incident. And today, I really wanna dig into, you know, both the incident itself, you know, your kind of reactions to it, the implications for a lot of this work going forward, and kind of what it reveals about the state of where we are today. You know, I think to to kick it off, maybe first, I'm curious just obviously, you know, you had your teammates go away for six days, firewalled off from from from you guys at the organization, and then at some point, they come back and and you get to read the report.
